written: Two Tenstorrent p150 cards, no NVIDIA anywhere.
spoken: Two Tenstorrent P one-fifty cards, no En-vidia anywhere.

written: The plan: replace the GPUs in my home AI server, and see how far these cards get with a real coding model.
spoken: The plan: replace the G P Us in my home A I server, and see how far these cards get with a real coding model.

written: That's episode one. First, install them.
spoken: That's episode one. First, install them.

written: Power on, the PSU shuts off.
spoken: [sighs] Power on, the P S U shuts off.

written: The card was powered through an adapter, from two PCIe cables.
spoken: The card was powered through an adapter, from two P C I express cables.

written: Without a power cable on the card, it still shuts off.
spoken: Without a power cable on the card, it still shuts off.

written: With an old Radeon in the same slot, everything works.
spoken: With an old Radeon in the same slot, everything works.

written: So the card must be shorting.
spoken: [frustrated] So the card must be shorting.

written: That logic felt airtight.
spoken: That logic felt airtight.

written: Second opinion: my desktop. It boots, the card's fans spin, and Windows never sees it.
spoken: Second opinion: my desktop. It boots, the card's fans spin, and Windows never sees it.

written: Card two: identical. Two dead cards!
spoken: [angry, frustrated] Card two: identical. Two dead cards!

written: I wrote the return ticket.
spoken: [sighs] I wrote the return ticket.

written: One last try, with the power supply's own cable instead of the adapter.
spoken: One last try, with the power supply's own cable instead of the adapter.

written: It boots! The card shows up, healthy!
spoken: [laughs] It boots! The card shows up, healthy!

written: The adapter was the problem the whole time. Of course, my power supply's maker said so. But who believes them?
spoken: The adapter was the problem the whole time. Of course, my power supply's maker said so. But who believes them?

written: My own research had said an approved adapter was fine.
spoken: My own research had said an approved adapter was fine.

written: Lesson one of this channel: read the manual. Not the one for the shiny new card. The one for the boring power supply you already own.
spoken: Lesson one of this channel: read the manual. Not the one for the shiny new card. The one for the boring power supply you already own.

written: While I was at it, I updated the card's firmware and power-cycled the server.
spoken: While I was at it, I updated the card's firmware and power-cycled the server.

written: And one thing I couldn't find anywhere online: the card runs fine on PCIe Gen 3.
spoken: And one thing I couldn't find anywhere online: the card runs fine on P C I express Gen three.

written: My CPU can't do more.
spoken: My C P U can't do more.

written: When the model is already in memory, loading it onto the card takes eleven seconds.
spoken: When the model is already in memory, loading it onto the card takes eleven seconds.

written: On Gen 5 it would barely change: only about three of those seconds are the link itself.
spoken: On Gen five it would barely change: only about three of those seconds are the link itself.

written: From my SSD it takes about three minutes, because the SSD is the slow part, not the slot.
spoken: From my S S D it takes about three minutes, because the S S D is the slow part, not the slot.

written: The model is Fish Audio Drama 3: thirty-six billion parameters, but only about three billion work for each slice of sound.
spoken: The model is Fish Audio Drama three: thirty-six billion parameters, but only about three billion work for each slice of sound.

written: Squeezed to four bits, it fits on one card.
spoken: Squeezed to four bits, it fits on one card.

written: Nobody had published a run of it on Tenstorrent, so Claude Code and I ported it in seven days.
spoken: Nobody had published a run of it on Tenstorrent, so Claude Code and I ported it in seven days.

written: What broke: the server's disk corrupted a weight file, a stale library path crashed the compiler, and a faster setting for the expert math filled a layer with garbage, so it stayed off.
spoken: What broke: the server's disk corrupted a weight file, a stale library path crashed the compiler, and a faster setting for the expert math filled a layer with garbage, so it stayed off.

written: Day one: the original model on the CPU, one layer at a time, as a reference. Day two: every weight mapped and checked against it.
spoken: Day one: the original model on the C P U, one layer at a time, as a reference. Day two: every weight mapped and checked against it.

written: On day three, the first eight test lines took fourteen point seven seconds for every second of speech.
spoken: On day three, the first eight test lines took fourteen point seven seconds for every second of speech.

written: What worked: one traced pass through the network for every frame, the audio decoder in a single trace, sampling on the card, a cached voice prompt, and the codec on the card as well.
spoken: What worked: one traced pass through the network for every frame, the audio decoder in a single trace, sampling on the card, a cached voice prompt, and the codec on the card as well.

written: I kept the four-bit weights, and by the end of day four the card needed zero point eight five seconds for every second of speech.
spoken: I kept the four-bit weights, and by the end of day four the card needed zero point eight five seconds for every second of speech.

written: On day six the card spoke this whole narration, and weak lines got another take. On day seven I froze the code.
spoken: On day six the card spoke this whole narration, and weak lines got another take. On day seven I froze the code.

written: Seven days on one card: this is what broke, and this is what worked.
spoken: Seven days on one card: this is what broke, and this is what worked.

written: On my test lines the card needs zero point eight five seconds for every second of speech, and zero point nine six over the whole narration, at about fifty-seven watts for the chip and one hundred and eighty for the whole board.
spoken: On my test lines the card needs zero point eight five seconds for every second of speech, and zero point nine six over the whole narration, at about fifty-seven watts for the chip and one hundred and eighty for the whole board.

written: Whisper's transcript matches the script at ninety-four percent. With today's live settings, including some custom kernels, my card needs about zero point five four.
spoken: Whisper's transcript matches the script at ninety-four percent. With today's live settings, including some custom kernels, my card needs about zero point five four.

written: The original model on a rented RTX Pro 6000 is about three times faster. Its memory is three and a half times faster, but that's not the whole story: my card isn't at its own memory limit yet.
spoken: The original model on a rented RTX Pro 6000 is about three times faster. Its memory is three and a half times faster, but that's not the whole story: my card isn't at its own memory limit yet.

written: And whether it sounds like me: you decide. Except for my intro and that one part, every word you heard was spoken by the card.
spoken: And whether it sounds like me: you decide. Except for my intro and that one part, every word you heard was spoken by the card.

written: And one card is already fast enough to speak in real time.
spoken: And one card is already fast enough to speak in real time.

written: Next episode: both cards, one coding model, and a fifteen-thousand-euro GPU to beat.
spoken: Next episode: both cards, one coding model, and a fifteen-thousand-euro G P U to beat.

written: So, did we exit the moat?
spoken: So, did we exit the moat?

written: We found the door, and it was a power cable.
spoken: We found the door, and it was a power cable.

written: For the voice of a YouTube video: yes. For an audiobook: probably. For a service helpdesk: not yet. Important parts are still missing.
spoken: For the voice of a YouTube video: yes. For an audiobook: probably. For a service helpdesk: not yet. Important parts are still missing.
